The bill would remove four outdated laws from the Agriculture portfolio.
It would repeal the Australian Meat and Live-stock Corporation Amendment Act 1990, the National Residue Survey (Consequential Provisions) Act 1992, and the Wool International Privatisation Act 1999.
The explanatory memorandum says removing obsolete laws gives businesses and individuals more certainty about their current regulatory duties.
Repeals the Australian Meat and Live-stock Corporation Amendment Act 1990.
Repeals the National Residue Survey (Consequential Provisions) Act 1992.

Businesses, individuals and community organisations that are subject to the Agriculture portfolio's regulations.
